pages.excerpt:
The**Office of the Prime Minister**, officially**Presidency of the Government**([Spanish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_language):*Presidencia del Gobierno*) is the[Spanish government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_government)structure that groups all the departments and officials that are at the service of the[prime minister](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Spain)to fulfil its constitutional duties.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Office_of_the_Prime_Minister_(Spain)#cite_note-4)It is staffed by a mix of career[civil servants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_servants)and[advisers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adviser). The highest-ranking official within the Office is the[Chief of Staff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moncloa_Chief_of_Staff), which is a political appointment on which the rest of the Office officials depend.
